plugin.name: On - full experience (recommended)
plugin.description:
Hair and tails get collision capsules and react to your hands and weapons — on both Faster HDT-SMP and HDT-SMP Flex.
Cost is bounded: only the 2 NPCs nearest you (within ~10 m) carry live rigs, and a closer NPC takes the slot from a farther one. A dense wig is 85-200 physics bodies, which is exactly why that budget exists.
You can tune it later in PPB_tuning.txt: npcRigMaxActors (how many NPCs), npcRigRangeU (the range), npcFollower 0 (kill switch, takes effect within a second, no restart).

plugin.name: Off - performance
plugin.description:
No hair or tail rigs at all: NPC hair and tails will NOT react to your touch, and your hand passes through them. Everything else in PPB is unaffected (body capsules, joints, touch detection on the body, heel fix).
Pick this on a machine that struggles in crowds. It installs the same PPB_tuning.txt with one line changed: npcFollower 0.
You can change your mind any time by editing that line back to 1 — no reinstall needed, it takes effect within a second, even mid-game.

plugin.name: On (recommended)
plugin.description:
NPCs react physically when you push them with your hands or a weapon.
Choosing On opens a page where you pick which reactions you want, one by one: - Push walk: a steady press makes the NPC step back. - Push stumble: a firm push makes the NPC stagger. - Shove knockdown: a hard shove knocks the NPC to the ground. - Leg sweep knockdown: sweeping the NPC's feet knocks them down.
Busy NPCs are always left alone: anyone sitting, sleeping, working at a crafting station or doing a chore, fighting, or in a kill move. NPCs leaning on a wall, rail or counter can't be pushed (they are braced), but their legs can still be swept.

plugin.name: Off
plugin.description:
Your hands and weapons never push, stagger or knock down an NPC, and sweeping their legs does nothing. All four push reactions are off, whatever the next page would have said.
The rest of PPB works as usual: body collision, touch sensing, the heel fix, and equip gestures if you keep them. You can change this later with bPushShove in SKSE/Plugins/PPB.ini. The change applies within a second, even mid-game.

plugin.name: On (recommended)
plugin.description:
Dress and undress NPCs with your hands: - Equip: hold a piece of clothing or armour against the matching part of the NPC's body for about a second, then let go. It goes on them, and it stays on (their outfit won't swap it back). - Undress: grab something the NPC is wearing with both hands and pull it off.
If that slot is already taken, the item falls instead of silently replacing what they wear. No messages pop up on screen.
Choosing On opens a page with one more choice: the outfit re-dress fix.

plugin.name: Off
plugin.description:
Holding clothing or armour against an NPC won't equip it, and pulling with both hands won't undress them. Pick this if another mod handles equipping by hand for you (for example Gift by Hand).
You can change this later with bEquipGestures in SKSE/Plugins/PPB.ini. This one is read when the game loads, so it needs a restart.

plugin.name: On (recommended)
plugin.description:
Captive and prisoner mods freeze an NPC in place with SetDontMove. In VR that freeze breaks the first time she is knocked down: she keeps playing a walk against a body that cannot move, and slides on the spot. This is the "moonwalk".
On: PPB refuses that freeze on the NPCs it drives (people only; the player, creatures and horses are never touched). On its own this lets a captive walk free instead of moonwalking. A restraint mod that works with PPB can then keep her in place with physics instead, so she still stands, falls and gets back up like anyone else.
Captives who are restrained (SetRestrained) stay restrained either way - PPB never removes that.
You can change this later with bSetDontMoveGuard in SKSE/Plugins/PPB.ini. The change applies within a second, even mid-game.

plugin.name: Off
plugin.description:
Captive and prisoner mods freeze NPCs exactly as they do without PPB, and a captive knocked down while frozen can moonwalk.
Note: a restraint mod that works with PPB and depends on this fix turns it back on when it is installed, whatever you pick here.
The rest of PPB works as usual. You can change this later with bSetDontMoveGuard in SKSE/Plugins/PPB.ini. The change applies within a second, even mid-game.

group.name: PCW (beta) - physics on your other CPU cores

plugin.name: On (recommended)
plugin.description:
BETA. Each woman who has PPB's Havok breast (the next choice) gets a private physics world of her own, a PCW, stepped on your other CPU cores instead of the game's physics thread. Her breast reacts to your hands, weapons and held objects exactly as it does in the game's physics.
Today the PCW carries the Havok breast. Havok Converter (optional, coming later) will move converted hair and clothes into the same world, which is where most of the saving comes from. You do not need it for this beta.
Needs Engine Fixes VR with bOverrideHavokMemorySystem = true in its EngineFixes.toml. Without it PPB writes why in PPB.log and the breast runs in the game's physics instead; nothing else changes.
Testers: type pcwab in the console once (about 4 minutes, standing still near your followers) and send the log files listed on the beta page.
You can change this later in SKSE/Plugins/PPB_tuning.txt: rigWorld 0, pcwOne 0 and sbWorld 1 turn it off (rigWorld 1, pcwOne 2, sbWorld 2 = on). The change applies within a second, even mid-game.

plugin.name: Off
plugin.description:
No private physics worlds. If you keep the Havok breast, it runs in the game's own physics, on the game's physics thread. Everything else in PPB is unaffected.
Pick this if a stutter or crash goes away with the PCW off - and please tell us, with your logs.
It installs the same PPB_tuning.txt with three lines changed: rigWorld 0, pcwOne 0, sbWorld 1. Set them back to 1, 2, 2 any time; the change applies within a second, even mid-game.

plugin.name: On (recommended)
plugin.description:
PPB builds its own Havok breast physics for every woman on a PPB skeleton (human, elf, orc, Yvanni, khajiit, argonian).
A touch dents the breast, a firmer push moves it, and a deeper push moves her. It collides with your hands, the objects you hold and Havok hair.
With PCW (beta) On it runs in her private physics world on your other CPU cores; with PCW (beta) Off, in the game's own physics.
It drives CBBE / 3BA bodies (and their outfits) and GT Softbody bodies. While a woman has it, her CBPC breast physics are paused and GT Softbody's breast XML is switched to a kinematic copy. Both are given back when she has none.
You can change this later with bHavokBreast in SKSE/Plugins/PPB_Options.ini. The change applies within a second, even mid-game.
Kinematic physics file derived from GT Softbody by Goutou (Nexus 152103), used with credit under its modification permission.

plugin.name: Off
plugin.description:
PPB builds no breast physics of its own: your own breast physics (CBPC, SMP, GT Softbody) run exactly as before.
The PCW (beta) choice is not changed by this one. With no Havok breast and no Havok Converter, the PCW has nothing to carry yet.
The rest of PPB works as usual. You can change this later with bHavokBreast in SKSE/Plugins/PPB_Options.ini. The change applies within a second, even mid-game.

plugin.name: On (recommended)
plugin.description:
Press your hand or weapon steadily against an NPC and they step back, away from your hand, for as long as you keep pressing. They stop when you stop. This is the gentle end of pushing: moving someone out of your way.
PPB.ini key: bPushWalk. Applies within a second, even mid-game.

plugin.name: Off
plugin.description:
A steady press doesn't move the NPC. Your hand still collides with them and touch is still sensed, and the stumble, shove knockdown and leg sweep work as you choose below.
PPB.ini key: bPushWalk.

plugin.name: On (recommended)
plugin.description:
Push an NPC firmly enough to bend them backwards and they stumble: the game's own stagger animation, turned to match the direction you pushed from.
If you turn Shove knockdown off but keep this on, a hard shove also makes them stumble instead of falling.
PPB.ini key: bPushStumble. Applies within a second, even mid-game.

plugin.name: Off
plugin.description:
A firm push never makes an NPC stagger. The walk, shove knockdown and leg sweep are not affected.
PPB.ini key: bPushStumble.

plugin.name: On (recommended)
plugin.description:
Shove an NPC hard and they're knocked off their feet: they go limp (ragdoll), fall, and get back up on their own.
PPB.ini key: bShoveRagdoll. Applies within a second, even mid-game.

plugin.name: Off
plugin.description:
A shove never knocks an NPC down. With Push stumble on, a hard shove makes them stumble instead. With both off, a hard shove does nothing.
This does NOT turn off the leg sweep. That is its own choice, below.
PPB.ini key: bShoveRagdoll.

plugin.name: On (recommended)
plugin.description:
Sweep or lift an NPC's feet off the floor with your hand or a weapon and they fall (ragdoll), like a real person would. Both feet have to leave the floor: lifting one leg while the other stays planted doesn't trip them.
It never trips an NPC who runs at full speed, and not for half a second after an NPC is moved more than about 100 units at once (a follower mod's catch-up teleport); pushes wait that half second too.
This works on NPCs leaning on walls, rails or counters too: leaning braces them against a push, not against a sweep. It is also the part of push/shove most likely to clash with other physics or animation mods. If NPCs fall when they shouldn't, turn it off.
PPB.ini key: bFeetLift. Applies within a second, even mid-game.

plugin.name: Off
plugin.description:
Lifting or sweeping an NPC's feet never knocks them down. The walk, stumble and shove knockdown are not affected.
PPB.ini key: bFeetLift.

plugin.name: On (recommended)
plugin.description:
An NPC whose last piece of clothing you took off with the two-hand undress, or a generic NPC you dressed with a press-to-equip, is not re-dressed in her default outfit by the game until she wears something new.
PPB_Options.ini key: bOutfitGuard. It is set up when the game starts, so a change needs a game restart.

plugin.name: Off
plugin.description:
The game's own outfit rules apply: an NPC you undressed or dressed by hand can be put back in her default outfit by the game. The equip gestures themselves work as usual.
PPB_Options.ini key: bOutfitGuard. A change needs a game restart.

plugin.name: OStrands climax from PPB stroking + NPC decals
plugin.description:
REQUIRES OStrands 0.8.0 (0_OStrands.dll) and OStim Standalone or SexLab (OStrands' own requirement).
PPB raises your schlong while your hand is on it. With this installed, STROKING it - your hand travelling along the raised shaft - fills a meter; when it is full, OStrands climaxes you with its real semen simulation, outside any scene. Every actor near you is handed to OStrands as a collision body, so the fluid lands on them instead of passing through.
The spurts' path is also swept, and every NPC it reaches gets a semen decal (the game's own skinned decals, like blood).
How much stroking, the decal range and the rest are in SKSE/Plugins/PPB_OStrands.ini (hot: edits apply within a second).
ONE SETTING IN OSTRANDS: set [Semen] Enabled = true in OStrands_User.ini (or on its SKSE Menu Framework page). On "auto" without OCum, OStrands only allows semen in SexLab scenes.
Adds one plugin: PPB_OStrands.esp (three forms, no masters).

plugin.name: Dismembering Framework - VR freeze fix
plugin.description:
INSTALL THIS IF YOU USE DISMEMBERING FRAMEWORK. Skip it otherwise.
Fixes the hard freeze when one NPC dismembers another. That freeze is a thread deadlock: DF cuts on a worker thread that needs the SKSE task queue, while the main thread holds the same lock inside the death-frame gear-attach and skinning pass. It predates PPB.
This installs an override for DismemberingFramework.ini that turns DF's threaded hit processing OFF, which makes the deadlock structurally impossible. PPB then supplies the death confirmation DF loses that way, by calling DF's own public API on the main thread. DF keeps all of its own conditions, chances, sounds and limb physics.
The file is stock DF settings with exactly ONE value changed: bDeferredHitProcess = 0 (DF default: 1)
OVERWRITES: SKSE/Plugins/DismemberingFramework.ini — if you have tuned DF yourself, copy that one line into your own file instead of installing this.
If you use DF and do NOT apply this, open PPB_tuning.txt and set dgDeathCut 0, or you may get doubled cuts.
